Monday, March 7, 2022  7:00 PM  Council Chambers

In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493 and
proposed Resolution No. 2498, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing
directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference.
There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the
following ways:

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
811 4380 7318 Passcode: 417488. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 811 4380 7318 Passcode: 417488.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 811 4380
7318 Passcode: 417488.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MARCH 7, 2022

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Assembly Bill 361, this meeting was
held via teleconference.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler

  Commissioners Absent:  Carman

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY 7, 2022

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 7,
  2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 7A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210423; ADDRESS: 2266 CARRIAGE DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: JOE AND ALMA SALZETTI;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210424)
  to demolish the existing single family residence and construct a new one-story single
  family residence. A Minor Deviation (MD-210425) is requested for an increase of not more
  than ten percent (10%) in the maximum allowable lot coverage.

Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-210423. In 2020, the applicant received approval by the Planning Commission
for a proposal that included additions to the existing property. Due to the results of studies that

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 7, 2022
  1
 were done of the property, it was found that the proposed additions would be more costly than
demolishing and rebuilding. This new proposal would bring the property into compliance with the
existing residential development standards.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is recommending that the following be added to the
Conditions of Approval:

  1. That the applicant work with the City’s Maintenance Division to replace a Pepper Tree that
  will be removed in the City’s right of way. This tree is being removed due to the relocation
  of the driveway.

  2. That the utilities be undergrounded, as is required for new construction per the City’s
  municipal code.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that approval of this application would extinguish all previous
approvals under Planning Application No. PA-191209.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Planning Application No. PA-210423
subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report and the additional two conditions outlined in
the presentation.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if staff had heard from any neighbors with concerns about this
project. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the neighbor who was opposed to the previous
project, came to City Hall to review the plans and was satisfied that the revised proposal met the
setback requirement. No additional correspondence was received.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about the existing walls, which are on the property and extend
to the street. Joe Salzetti, Property Owner, stated that these walls could be removed if that is the
desire of the City. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City typically does not have issue
with this; if the Planning Commission would like to see this wall setback further from the street,
then this could be included as a condition of approval.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR expressed concern with camouflaging the air conditioning
condensers. Tim Racisz, Architect, stated that this will not be a problem.

VICE CHAIR YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210423 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OF APPROVAL OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL TWO
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE PRESENTATION, AND AN ADDITIONAL CONDITION
  TO SETBACK THE WALLS ALONG THE PROPERTY LINE, WHICH EXTEND TO THE
  CURB, TO A DISTANCE RECOMMENDED BY STAFF.

 AYES: Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson, Edler
 NOES:
 ABSENT: Carman
 ABSTAIN:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
Application No. PA-210423 with the conditions as stated. There is a 20-day appeal period by
which any member of the public or the City Council on its own motion may appeal the project.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the streetlights on Bart Earl Way between Beechgate
and the Red Onion are still not working. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City’s
Maintenance Department identified several lights that were not working and contacted SCE; she
will follow-up on this.

10.  MANAGER ITEMS

Planning Manager Naughton stated that The Residences at Rolling Hills Country Club and the
Rolling Hills Country Club projects are almost complete. If any Planning Commissioners are
interested, staff will be setting up one to two-hour tours of the project.

In response to a question by CHAIR SCHACHTER, Planning Manager Naughton stated that The
Residences is 100% sold.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, MARCH 7, 2022
  2
 VICE CHAIR YOO asked about school districting with this project. Planning Manager Naughton
stated that initially, there were residential lots in Torrance Unified School District, Palos Verdes
Peninsula Unified School District and Los Angeles Unified School District. All residential lots are
now within Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District, with the exception of two or three
residential lots that have remained in the Los Angeles Unified School District; there are
disclosures associated with these properties for any future property owners.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, FEBRUARY 8, 2022

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered

 12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 7:33 p.m.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Robert Schachter, Chair
